Overview

Runs

This page is the EJ199 module’s record — with one caveat that frames every number: EJ199 is the wavelength-shifting carrier tuned to capture LuO:Yb emission, and the LuO:Yb crystals were not yet in hand. These runs measure the WLS-only baseline — expect dimmer, slower a priori, and that is what we find.

Response ~550 ADC-eq/GeV — the dimmest module (LuAG ~620, DSB1 ~1,350) — and timing ~1.7× slower than LuAG at 5 GeV, with the trend fitting pure photostatistics (σ_t ≈ 1360/√E ps, constant term unresolved): both are the expected signature of the WLS carrier running without its LuO:Yb light source, where the shifter’s own re-emission time and reduced light yield dominate. These three points are the baseline the crystal-loaded module will be compared against. Tag plateaus (88.7/22.8/5.6%) match DSB1’s to a fraction of a percent — the beam is reproducible across all three modules. Negative-beam points (−7/−9/−11 GeV) follow.

Run-specific notes

everything unique to this run

First EJ199 beam. Tag plateau 88.7% (17,732 e). Miss 69.5% (1 GeV material floor). Timing reflects the missing fast component: t-MEDIAN 1367 ± 24 ps — the WLS re-emission delay with no LuO:Yb light to shift.

Run-specific notes

everything unique to this run

Tag plateau 5.6% (1,121 e). Miss 12.0%. Scan point (ΣLG > 1200): peak 2740 ± 74 — ~550 ADC-eq/GeV, the dimmest module (LuAG ~620, DSB1 ~1,350) — and t-MEDIAN 380 ± 18 ps (LuAG 228, DSB1 156). Both exactly as expected for the WLS carrier without its LuO:Yb crystals: this run is the baseline the crystal-loaded module will be measured against.
